turns.assessment: The outage is a network-wide optical failure rather than a client-port or single-channel fault: many services and lightpaths failed simultaneously, while the common dependency is roadm.S06. Concurrent AMP_INPUT_LOS on two different OMSs leaving S06 (toward S19 and S21) localizes the loss to the S06 ROADM before those branches. A failed WSS input port can block the common arriving channel set and thereby remove channels from multiple outgoing degrees; separate span, booster, or connector faults would require coincident failures on both outgoing lines.

proposals.rationale: roadm.S06 is the sole listed common dependency, and simultaneous all-channel optical loss downstream on multiple S06 outgoing degrees is consistent with a common WSS input-port failure there.

A disconnected optical patch at S06 could cause hard loss, but an OMS input patch normally affects only one outgoing degree and therefore does not naturally explain both outbound AMP_INPUT_LOS alarms.

proposals.rationale: A switch failure could interrupt many ODUs, but it would produce ODU-layer failures rather than loss of optical channels and amplifier input light on multiple OMSs.

clarify.assessment: The evidence localizes the fault to a WSS input-port failure at roadm.S06, but it does not identify which incoming degree failed. The downstream losses on multiple outgoing degrees are compatible with any of the four resolved input ports, and the unchanged upstream monitoring does not distinguish them because a WSS port failure occurs after that monitoring point.
